phrases.text: So welcome back again.
It's time to solve one more problem.
Now in this problem, we are given that a train crosses a pole in twelve seconds
and a one hundred and eighty-meter platform in twenty-four seconds.
The question is asking us to find the length of the train.
Let the length of the train be L meter.
Since the train is moving at the same speed in both cases,
its speed will be equal in both situations.
Now let us first write the speed when the train crosses the pole.
When a train crosses a pole,
distance covered is only the length of train.
So
speed equals length of train divided by time to cross pole.
Speed equals L divided by twelve.
Call this Equation 1.
Now let us write the speed when the train crosses the platform.
Here the train has to cross both its own length and the platform.
So the total distance becomes length of train plus length of platform.
That is L plus one hundred and eighty. Hence, speed equals L plus one hundred and eighty divided by twenty-four. Call this Equation 2.
Now this is the important point.
The train is the same and it is moving at the same speed.
So Equation 1 and Equation 2 must be equal.
Therefore,
L divided by twelve equals L plus one hundred and eighty
divided by twenty-four. After simplifying this whole equation, L equals one hundred and eighty meter.
Hence, the length of the train is one hundred and eighty meter. So the correct answer is option D.
